chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan and Fadalah, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who forgot the Tawaf al-Nisa' until he returned to his family. He said: Women do not become lawful for him until he visits the House. If he dies, then his guardian or someone else should perform it on his behalf. But as long as he is alive, it is not valid that it be performed on his behalf. And if he forgot the jamarat, the two are not equal: indeed, the throwing is a sunnah (prophetic tradition), while the tawaf is an obligation.

key_terms.الْجِمَارَ: the stone pillars targeted in the rite of throwing during hajj
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: a prescribed sunnah (prophetic tradition) act, not equal here to an obligation
key_terms.طَوَافَ النِّسَاءِ: the tawaf after which women become lawful again to the pilgrim
key_terms.فَرِيضَةٌ: an obligatory act that must be fulfilled
key_terms.لَا تَحِلُّ لَهُ النِّسَاءُ: women do not become lawful for him for marital relations
key_terms.وَلِيُّهُ: his guardian, who may fulfill it on his behalf after death
key_terms.يَزُورَ الْبَيْتَ: he visits the Sacred House to perform the required tawaf

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on someone who forgets Tawaf al-Nisa' and returns to his family before performing it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who forgets Tawaf al-Nisa' and returns to his family before performing it. It states that marital relations remain forbidden until he performs the tawaf himself, and distinguishes this obligation from the throwing of the jamarat, which is treated here as sunnah (prophetic tradition) rather than an obligatory rite of the same level.
